t: You're looking at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, on Queen Square. It was the first hospital in England dedicated entirely to diseases of the nervous system. It sits beside the UCL Institute of Neurology on the same site, and together they form a major centre for neuroscience research. Several people died here, including Dame Juliet Rhys-Williams, a writer and politician who moved between the Liberal and Conservative parties, and John Hobson, a Conservative politician. Megan Bhari, who founded a charity, also died here, aged just twenty-three.
